title: Quiet O in OUS
kidRule: When a describing word ends with an 'us' sound, like ENORMOUS, the ending is usually spelled O-U-S. We cannot hear the O, but it has to be there!
hint: This describing word ends with an 'us' sound, but a quiet letter is hiding in that ending. Can you find it?
reminder: Describing words that end with an 'us' sound are spelled O-U-S, with a quiet O before the U.

check.question: Why does ENORMOUS end with O-U-S and not just U-S?
check.correctAnswer: Because describing words that end with an 'us' sound are usually spelled O-U-S!
distractors: Because the first O needs a twin near the end
Because every word needs two vowels next to each other

words.sent: An enormous whale splashed beside our boat.
words.story: A blue whale's heart is enormous: it is about as big as a bumper car!
words.card: *Norm* the snail ordered an *enormous* pizza and ate it for a whole year!

words.def: Feeling worried or a little scared about something.
words.sent: I felt nervous before my first swimming lesson.
words.story: The fluttery 'butterflies in your tummy' feeling is real! When you are nervous, your body gets ready for action and your stomach slows down.
words.card: The turkey looked *nervous* when it was invited to din*ner*!

words.def: Able to hurt you; not safe.
words.sent: It is dangerous to cross the road without looking.
words.story: The golden poison frog is only about two inches long, but the poison in its skin makes it one of the most dangerous animals in the rainforest!
words.card: The *danger* sign said: '*Dangerous* tickle monster ahead!'

words.def: Feeling unhappy because someone else has something you want.
words.sent: My cat gets jealous when I pet the dog.
words.story: Dogs can get jealous too! In one study, dogs pushed and nudged their owners when the owners petted a toy dog.
words.card: The s*eal* felt *jealous* of the walrus and his fancy mustache!

words.sent: Grandpa cooked a fabulous dinner for us.
words.story: The word comes from 'fable', so long ago it meant something so amazing that it belonged in a story!
words.card: The *bul*ldog wore a *fabulous* purple wig to the dog show!

words.def: So good that it fills you with wonder.
words.sent: We had a marvelous time at the fair.
words.story: Hummingbirds are marvelous fliers: they can hover in one spot and even fly backward!
words.card: I *marvel* at the *marvelous* moose who can juggle muffins!

words.def: Wanting to know or learn about something.
words.sent: The curious kitten peeked inside the paper bag.
words.story: A robot car exploring Mars is named Curiosity, and the name was picked by a 12-year-old girl who won a contest!
words.card: The *curious* pig with the *cur*ly tail opened every door in the barn!

words.def: Happy to share or give to others.
words.sent: It was generous of Mia to share her snack.
words.story: Vampire bats are surprisingly generous: a bat that has found food will share its meal with a hungry friend!
words.card: *Gene* the squirrel is so *generous* that he gave away his very last acorn!

words.def: Very big, very strong, or very good.
words.sent: The thunder made a tremendous boom.
words.story: A bolt of lightning has tremendous heat: it is about five times hotter than the surface of the sun!
words.card: Ten *men* made a *tremendous* splash when they jumped into the pool together!

words.def: So silly that it makes you laugh.
words.sent: The clown wore a ridiculous hat shaped like a fish.
words.story: The word comes from an old Latin word that means 'to laugh'!
words.card: I can't get *rid* of this *ridiculous* chicken on my head!
